Gallagher said the SoE Dean senior leadership team is reviewing several student-group sponsorship requests and will respond after Thanksgiving.

Treat as a claim to verify before paying or replying.

title: Spokes 27 - Edgerton first meeting
summary: Gloria Ma asked Justin Schmidt for a first meeting. Justin replied Nov 24 2026 with a Microsoft Bookings link for a meeting with him and Marvelin (pick a slot the week of Nov 30 or later) and one task: choose a team safety officer as his safety point of contact.

title: Please Run MVR for MIT SPOKES 2027 Team
summary: On Nov 24 2026 Marvelin asked MIT Background Check to run MVR (motor vehicle record) checks for seven Spokes 2027 members (all but Olivia Girand) so they can drive MIT rentals; results go to her and are redistributed.

title: Day -53: Warming up for the Summer ☀️
summary: Pre-season update: the 7 team bikes were built by Trek and picked up for first test rides, the route was finalized, and the crowdfunding goal was still $50k. Learning-festival workshops (motors, electricity, 3D modeling, chemical reactions) were being prepped.

title: Day -1: Government Operation
summary: Packing day in the Boston area: the team fit bikes, camping gear, and LF supplies into a rented cargo van and a minivan, and spent hours rigging the roof storage bag, which needed a different strap setup than the 2025 method. They slept around 3 AM before a 6 AM departure for DC.

title: Day 0: Half a Mile of Hell
summary: Drove from Boston to DC in the minivan and cargo van. Roof straps slammed the windows and the dashboard alarmed on the unbuckled middle seat until they fixed it. They arrived around 7:30 PM and spent the night precutting felt, cardboard and paper for the next day's festival.

title: Day 1: Small Wins
summary: First learning festival at the DC Youth Services Center, a juvenile rehab facility. The team ran seven rotations of the Lego electric-motor workshop; only some students got motors working, though one class of boys all did.

title: Day 2: First SAG (and 2nd and 3rd and 4th)
summary: Rode 88.6 miles from DC to Linden VA after a late, sleep-deprived start. Nate missed a turn and rode a four-lane highway with no shoulder before SAGging about 6 miles; Aarushi, Nunu and Caroline were SAG'd at mile 76.

title: Day 3: Pool & Pool
summary: Short 31.8-mile ride from Linden to Luray VA. A stranger, Jimmy Baker, donated $1,000 at a gas-pump rest stop, and a pizza place donated pizzas after a phone call. The team stayed at a campground with a pool.

title: Day 4: Country Roads, Take Me Home…
summary: Rode 62.5 miles from Luray to Waynesboro VA along the Shenandoah. Tents, bike shoes and laundry left out overnight were soaked with dew, and the team stopped at a picnic oasis for a long lunch. Host Pam picked them up over the mountain to her Shannon Farm home.

title: Day 5: Floatin' Along
summary: Rest day at Pam's Shannon Farm: the team slept in, played card games, floated on the community lake on a 7-person floatie, and attended Pam's potluck. A spider was found in one cabin's bed.

title: Day 6: Kids and Bugs
summary: Learning festival at the Fluvanna County Public Library with about 70 kids: chemistry for middle and high schoolers, felt-monster genetics for kindergarteners. Afterward two riders waited 30 minutes at a community center a mile away until someone drove them back.

title: Day 7: Dear Nate
summary: Rode 41.9 miles from Waynesboro to Lexington VA after a borrowed-truck shuttle to the route start. Two riders spent over an hour at urgent care and a CVS pharmacy waiting on a prescription signature. Host Dirk took the team to the river that evening.

title: Day 8: A Love Letter to My Team
summary: Rode 67.5 miles from Lexington to Roanoke VA. A rider's chain kept falling off, and the team spent a 3-hour evening meeting working out how ride pace and priorities should fit together.

title: Day 9: Hopeful Wanderers
summary: Rode 40.5 miles from Roanoke to Blacksburg VA, plus a hike up McAfee Knob. Host Steve rode the first 20 miles, and the final 750 ft climb in 3 miles led to host Ann's house.

title: Day 10: another nate blog where half the team gets SAG'd out
summary: Rode 83 miles from Blacksburg to Tazewell VA. Aarushi hit a pothole and crashed into a tree; Hokie Spokes in Blacksburg fully repaired her bike the same day. Riders sheltered from a storm at a Narrows church, and Nunu was SAG'd at mile 65 for knee pain.

title: Day 11: Playlist Across America
summary: Small-town learning festival at the Tazewell United Methodist Church: iodine color-change chemistry for older kids and felt-monster genetics for little kids. Afterward Aarushi and Tatiana joined the church women's group, and Aarushi started a playlist of songs from people they met.

title: Day 12: Big A(hh) Mountain
summary: Rode 72.6 miles from Tazewell to Breaks Interstate Park VA, climbing Big A Mountain. The route passed a no-trespassing gate after a last-minute change, plus several dogs. Dinner was free in Elkhorn City KY, and the team camped at the park.

title: Day 13: Let me get a bite of that
summary: Caroline was bitten by a loose dog on a back road leaving Breaks Interstate Park. The team waited hours for the rescue squad, sheriff and an ambulance, Caroline and Aarushi went to Pikeville Medical Center, and the whole team then SAG'd to Hazard KY.

title: Day 14: Where do we go from here?
summary: Taught at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard KY to a talented group of kids. After the festival, the team had a planning meeting about whether to keep biking through dog country and decided to rent a pickup truck so any rider could be shuttled.

title: Day 15: Dog Days Are Over?
summary: Rode 78.9 miles from Hazard to London KY with a follow car shadowing the riders and mace ready for dogs. A pickup reservation made online was not honored at the counter, and Tatiana sprained her ankle in the dark at the host's home.

title: Day 16: the new normal
summary: Slept in a patched-together hammock setup at Lucy and Steve's in London KY, which was cold and poor for sleep. Rode 64.8 miles to Liberty KY through 6-8 dogs, and Tatiana needed three hospitals to get her sprain X-rayed.

title: Day 17: Fake it till you make it
summary: The injured driver drove the van while riders covered 88.8 miles from Liberty to a campground at Mammoth Cave KY. Stops included a waterfall at Brush Creek Baptist Church, a dinner at Farmwald's Dutch Bakery and Deli, and a donated dinner at La Cabana.

title: Day 18: BUSS*-EEs
summary: Returned the extra rental pickup early and lost camping items (two pillows, a sleeping pad, a camp chair, a hammock and a blanket) off the minivan's roof bag on I-65. The team toured Mammoth Cave, stopped at Buc-ee's, then biked 35.6 miles to Bowling Green, where Airbnbs were donated.

title: Day 19: Mogcoaster 🎢
summary: Rest day in Bowling Green: Noah (Tatiana's boyfriend) arrived after a 10-hour drive. The team spent the day at Beech Bend waterpark and amusement park using a group season-pass discount.

title: Day 20: we the people
summary: Taught the largest LF so far, about 100 kids in groups of 25 at the WKU Innovation Campus in Bowling Green. Afterward Howard's Bike Shop re-measured and realigned Aarushi's bike for free, and the team had a late-night downtown outing.

title: Day 21: Alternate Reality
summary: Rode 87 miles from Bowling Green to a church in Madisonville KY. The team left about 90 minutes late after a late night, rode together for the first 24 miles, and napped at lunch. Sleeping bags and pads smelled badly from the roof storage.

title: Day 22: A Stench and A Storm
summary: Rode 81.8 miles from Madisonville KY to Harrisburg IL in rain for the first 20 miles and before lunch. After crossing the Ohio River, the team cut a 7-mile detour that the 2025 route had added for an ice cream shop. Brad and Sherri hosted the team in Harrisburg.

title: Day 23: everything except biking
summary: Slow start (left around 9am) after a rest-plus-learning-festival stretch, then a short flat 52-mile ride to Murphysboro IL with many detours: a pet rescue thrift store, a BBQ shop, an art store, a cafe and an antique store. The group rode the last 20 miles at about 18 mph.

title: Day 24: 100 Things I Love About Spokes
summary: First century (101.1 miles) from Murphysboro IL to St. Louis MO, leaving by 7am, a team record start. Rest stops at a Lutheran church, a Dairy Queen and a coffee shop; the last stretch ran on the paved Metro Bike Link Trail past the Gateway Arch.

title: Day 25: Unreliable Narrator
summary: Morning in St. Louis with a Forest Park tour from host Alex, then a Missouri ride on the Katy Trail. Caroline SAG'd out with an elbow nerve injury; a storm stranded the group near Augusta MO for about two hours, and Nate SAG'd the rest of the team to a pizza dinner and an Airbnb on the Katy Trail.

title: Day 26: To Journal or To Blog…
summary: Caroline took a rest day for her elbow and Nunu went to urgent care in Jefferson City for chafing, so three bikes went on a weak hitch. Drew's tire was slashed; the team put a wheel from Caroline's unused bike on his bike and took the damaged wheel to a bike shop before it closed. The group reached Vince's in Columbia MO at 9pm.

title: Day 27: somewhere in between
summary: Carmen reflects on the team's 'speed demon vs sidequester' split and argues for balance. The group took a long sidequest (peaches, an art gallery, a casino stop and a Boonville festival), then rode into a storm, and a collision between Nunu and Nate at a turn broke two screens. They ended at Dave and Shandra's house in Marshall MO.

title: Day 28: Sunrise to Sunset
summary: Forecast of 107-degree 'feels like' heat and 30 mph crosswinds led to a 4am wake and a 5:30am start on a route with about 5,000 ft of climbing, which was not flat as they expected. The double draft line broke on the climbs and the team was exhausted at the second rest stop. They reached a Kansas City hotel around 3pm.

title: Day 29: Tyranny of the Majority
summary: Rest day in Kansas City: a hotel breakfast, a Barnes and Noble stop, Shake Shack, Auntie Anne's, a free yoga class arranged by Aarushi, and a Netherlands vs Morocco World Cup watch party that ended in a penalty shootout loss for the Netherlands.

title: Day 30: a glimpse of the outside world
summary: Learning festival at aSTEAM Village in Kansas City MO drew only 15 students, far below the usual 60 to 80. The team then ran a mini-LF for an absent student, ate at Joe's BBQ near a World Cup watch party, and spent the night at a laundromat that was an ordeal with the tents.

title: Day 31: Don't Overlook Overbrook
summary: Crossed into Kansas, rode through Kansas City's quieter west side, and detoured around a road closure using the square road grid. Tatiana and Caroline each got a flat on gravel, the team skipped the last rest stop, and Tatiana bonked before reaching Scott's house in Overbrook KS for burgers and pickleball.

title: Day 32: the flattest thing in kansas is our tires
summary: Breakfast with the retirees at Scott's Overbrook community, then a flat-tire day: the team logged seven flats in about 24 hours, including Caroline's, Carmen's twice, and a passing cyclist's tire. After Osage City stops they rode a headwind slog to 12th Avenue Baptist Church in Emporia KS.

title: Day 33: life is a highway (50)
summary: Snooze-heavy late start (about 9:40am) and a ride on US-50 with its wide shoulder. Stops included HeBrews CoffeeHouse in Cottonwood Falls, a minivan oil pan that dragged until a free fix, and a giant nail puncture on Aarushi's tire at a Dollar General before the group reached Janet and Orvin's in Newton KS.

title: Day 34: the semiquincentennial
summary: July 4 ride starting at 5am to beat 95-degree heat. The group shelter-stopped for about two hours at a Burrton KS gas station during a thunderstorm, then reached a Macksville KS church, after riding 92.6 miles on US-50 with a sandy stretch and cow fields.

title: Day 35: The Wickedest Little Bugs in America
summary: Mosquito-bitten team had breakfast with the Macksville Christian Church community, then rode 62.6 miles with tailwinds past hundreds of windmills and a halfway-point museum to Dodge City KS. Lunch ran from 4pm to 6pm and dinner with hosts Lindy and Warren was around 9pm.

title: Day 36: life is still a highway (50)
summary: A strong tailwind out of Dodge City made for fast riding. Aarushi's tube-equipped tire flatted again on US-50, so the team took a sandy gravel alternate route to avoid feedlots, and finished at a public pool outside Garden City before dinner at Victory Baptist Church in Lakin KS.

title: Day 37: welcome to colorful colorado
summary: Crossed into Colorado and rode a tailwind to Lamar. The lunch rest stop near the state line had aggressive flies, and a nap there turned into a 1.5-hour sleep. Lamar Christian Church housed them, and Lucy's Tacos donated 7 burritos. A bike lock cable knotted around a front axle had to be cut that night.

title: Day 38: So… steak for dinner?
summary: Learning festival at the Lamar Community Building with 30 students aged 4 to 15 across four groups, a Rock-Paper-Scissors-Rockstar opener, and a pizza lunch in the gym. The day ended with a steakhouse dinner funded by a $20-per-person credit and a Zumba class, and a Tractor Supply loan of wire cutters fixed the lock cable.

title: Day 39: The Spokes Routine
summary: Routine-focused post that walks through the team's daily schedule and rest-stop tour: Valley Grocery, a Dairy Queen with Tony's fruit stand, a La Junta public pool, a storm shelter at McDonald's and Wendy's, and Knapps Farm Market in Rocky Ford. The team reached Trinity Lutheran Church in Fowler CO into the sunset after a fourth flat of the trip.

title: Day 40:🌵✈️😁⛰️🌦️🌈
summary: Aarushi shaved miles off the planned route (87.4 miles total), and the team detoured to the Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum. They crossed a dry stretch with no services, a boarded-up I-25 rest stop and a parallel trail, then ended at In-N-Out and an Airbnb in Colorado Springs shared with Aarushi's family.

title: Day 41: Emmenez-moi au bout de la terre
summary: Rest day in Colorado Springs: a home-cooked breakfast, a Pikes Peak drive (about three hours up and down) with a scream from the summit, a Garden of the Gods visit, and a mountain-bike ride at Red Rock Canyon by Drew and Carmen (an optional 9.6-mile ride).

title: Day 42: mooooooooo
summary: Left Colorado Springs for a long day into Denver (82.5 miles, 3,707 ft): a lakeside rest stop with volleyball and swimming, a mountain-bike detour through a cow pasture, a tea shop stop, and a flat on a climb. The day ended at MIT and Spokes alum hosts Kate and Manuel's house in Denver.

title: Day 43: The Warped Wall
summary: Largest climb of the trip so far (about 2,000 ft over 10 miles) out of Golden CO, after a Woody's Pizza lunch and a Clear Creek tubing run. Drew felt sick at the top and the team was winded and nauseated at altitude. The day ended at an Idaho Springs Airbnb after construction closures.

title: Day 44: MIT Paddles
summary: Rest day in Idaho Springs: a white water rafting and kayaking trip about 1.5 hours away (Class 2 rapids, with the kayaks spinning and flipping), a 30-foot cliff jump, and a food hall dinner. In the evening the team spent 2 to 3 hours on expense spreadsheets.

title: Day 45: I'm On Top of the World
summary: Crossed the Continental Divide over Loveland Pass (about 11,990 ft), with a steep final climb and a fast descent. Ashley and her family joined the team in Keystone. A storm around 8pm forced the group into a SAG, and Drew rode on alone through the storm to Breckenridge, where host Alison hosted dinner.

title: Day 46: 100 PICTURES ARE WORTH 100000 WORDS
summary: A 105.7-mile day from Breckenridge to Glenwood Springs CO, documented with a photo every 10 minutes. The scenery moved from mountains to canyon to desert, and the drivers switched at 2pm.

title: Day 47: hot springs and hot people
summary: Learning festival at the Glenwood Springs library, with four age groups building cardboard houses, animals and cacti. The evening included dinner and games with visiting Stanford Spokes riders, then a late-night natural hot spring.

title: Day 48: the menagerie
summary: Rode 47.6 miles from Glenwood Springs to Parachute, CO, a short day. A nail punctured Nunu's tire at the first rest stop, and Drew swapped back tires with her. The team also stopped at an alpaca farm and watched the World Cup third-place game at a sports bar in Rifle.

title: Day 49: MIT Soccer (fans)
summary: Rode 53.5 miles from Parachute to Grand Junction, CO, timed to reach a restaurant with a watch-party room for the World Cup final. The route sent riders onto an overgrown bike path to avoid the Highway 70 tunnel, and they stopped at a Palisade peach stand.

title: Day 50: 100 miles in 100 degrees
summary: Hot ride of 100+ degrees from Grand Junction toward Moab: the team ran out of ice, a driver had to drive back to Grand Junction for more, and riders had mild heat exhaustion. Riders swam in the Colorado River, a storm forced a turn back, and bikes were locked at a campground to finish the next morning. The route file listed 122.5 miles, but the actual ride was 87.9 miles.

title: Day 51: does it count as a rest day if we have to bike?
summary: Rode 32 miles from Hittle Bottom Campground back to Moab, unsupported, to finish the previous day's ride. That evening the team toured Canyonlands at dusk during thunderstorms and flash-flood warnings, found the park mostly empty, and had dinner donated at Arches Thai.

title: Day 52: I Spy 8 Breathtaking Arches
summary: Rest day in Moab. The team visited Arches National Park, hiking Delicate Arch (a hat blew off the trail and was rescued) and Double Arch, then bought metal water bottles at a Moab gear shop after plastic insulated bottles melted their ice. They ate a second burger at Milt's and bought matching shirts.

title: Day 53: Reliving History
summary: Moab to Green River State Park (55.6 miles). The 2026 route swapped I-70 for a gravel road to avoid an 80 mph highway. The driver stopped at Jackass Joe's, an alien-themed gas station at Exit 182 in Crescent Junction, UT, to refill water, and a dirt-road reroute at the highway corner was swamped with mud. The team camped at Green River State Park.

title: Day 54: maybe mars is a small town in utah
summary: Driver day for Caroline and Carmen. Riders covered about 95 miles from Green River State Park to Capitol Reef in heat and a thunderstorm wind, with about 13 miles on I-70. Tatiana, Drew and Caroline added extra loops for a century at Capitol Reef.

title: Day 55: Hello Down There
summary: Rest day at Capitol Reef: a 5-mile Grand Wash Trail walk and fresh pie at the campground pie shop. A park ranger turned the group back from the scenic drive because of flash-flood warnings. In the evening they went to the Torrey farmers market and the Bicknell International Film Festival's bad-movie screening.

title: Day 56: a series of reflections
summary: The trip's biggest climb, about 6,000 ft: from Capitol Reef through red rock, a wind-and-hail squall on a gravel climb, a cold lunch at 9,500 ft, and a 10,049 ft summit in the Dixie National Forest. Steep gravel descents led to a lake stop with kayaks, where two riders ran an hour late with no cell service. The team reached Escalante at dusk.

title: Day 57: What are Utah king about?
summary: Driver day for Drew: Escalante to Bryce Canyon (47.9 miles, about 3,960 ft). The riders faced an 18-mile opening climb, and Drew carried snacks up the hill. The last rest stop was a coffee shop beside a gas station that sells cheeseburgers. Nate's family hosted the team in an Airbnb near Bryce.

title: Day 58: we had a bryce day :)
summary: Rest day at Bryce Canyon with Nate's parents, who cooked meals and brought a birthday cake. The team hiked Sunrise Point and Wall Street (about 2 miles, 600 ft of gain). Dog repellent (pepper spray) leaked in a bike bag, and the residue survived two washes.

title: Day 59: The One Where "7 MIT Students" Almost Becomes "6 MIT Students"
summary: Bryce Canyon to Zion (100.3 miles, about 4,400 ft). Aarushi and Carmen rerouted the riders onto a Zion backcountry trail that was closed in places. Drew's bike went off a cliff in a rockslide, and he walked it down alone, reaching a shuttle stop after about 2 hours. Caroline's father shuttled four riders through the closed tunnel, and the team regrouped at Zion Lodge that night.

title: Day 60: An Ode To How Spokes Ended Up In Vegas
summary: Rest day in Zion, with a Walter's Wiggles hike and Angel's Landing summit by Carmen and Aarushi. The team then drove about 3 hours to Las Vegas, where Trek had a replacement bike ready for Drew the same day after several shops did not call back. They returned home around 1 am.

title: Day 61: A Tale of Two Cities
summary: Driver day for Caroline. The Narrows hike was cut short after about 1.5 miles, and Drew and Tatiana could not get through the Zion Lodge car gate. Caroline left early with family. The rest of the team rode from 3 to 10 pm in 100+ degree heat to finish in Cedar City (45.6 miles, about 3,700 ft), with a rider nearly passing out.

title: Day 62: Jesus for 300
summary: Cedar City to Milford (59.2 miles, 1,525 ft) in extreme heat. Carmen's twin sister rode until mile 22 and then got a ride back. The team slept inside a Milford church, where showers were hidden behind the chapel stage. Sprinklers hit the team's cowboy camp on the lawn around 12:40 am.

title: Day 63: Romanticizing the Mundane
summary: Milford to Baker, NV (84.9 miles, 4,539 ft), crossing into Nevada through long straight desert with climbs and crosswinds. Some riders went to Great Basin National Park for a lake swim, where Nate cut his foot on a sharp rock. The team stayed in a Baker church after dinner at Stargazer Inn.

title: Day 64: Is something burning?
summary: Drew was too sick to ride. The team called off the Baker to Ely ride (61.7 miles planned) after wildfire smoke reached 'very unhealthy' levels. Nunu drove Drew to Ely, where he ate a burger and recovered. The team stayed at the high school hosting them.

title: Day 65: The Legend of the Rider in White
summary: Learning festival at an Ely library from 11 am to 5 pm, not the usual 9 to 3; the team had forgotten the schedule. Drew and Nate ran an electric motors workshop, and the team had lunch from a burger place. That evening Nate rode the 36-mile ride skipped the day before, including an 8-mile, 2,000-ft climb, with Nunu driving support.

title: Day 66: POV I'm a Bike
summary: Ely to Eureka, NV (79.2 miles, 4,543 ft) on Highway 50. A rear tire popped early on the second stretch, so the support driver had to bring a replacement from Ely. Several riders got sick, and flies swarmed the food at rest stops. The team surprised Nate with a birthday stop. They stayed at a church 18 miles north of the route, reached by shuttle.

title: Day 67: Inside the Mind of One of This Generation's Greatest Thinkers
summary: Aarushi's voice-memo day on Highway 50 from Eureka, about 90 miles (3,698 ft), toward Mt. Airy, NV. The day included a sandy cattle-track detour the riders walked, a wrong turn, and a wildfire in the area. The team camped at a church and RV park concrete pad in Austin, NV, and left at 10 pm to ride overnight.

title: Day 68: Oh How am I Gonna Be an Optimist About This
summary: Overnight ride on Highway 50 from Mt. Airy to Fallon, NV (about 95 miles, 2,000 ft), starting at midnight. The team pulled over for about an hour of sleep on a tarp at about mile 60 and finished at a Fallon diner for breakfast. Some riders added miles to reach 200 total, and a virus was going around the team.

title: Day 69: just a biker gang of irresponsible youths
summary: Final learning festival at the Fallon Youth Club. Most signed-up kids cancelled because of school-supply pickup day, so the team taught one kid in the morning and four in the afternoon (chemistry, Monster Genome, electric motors). The team then donated leftover LF supplies to FYC.

title: Day 70: The Last Hurrah
summary: Left Fallon at 2:15 am for South Lake Tahoe (101.4 miles, 5,750 ft). Riders had a sunrise ride, a Carson City coffee-shop stop, and a flat for Drew near the foot of the climb. They climbed about 2,000 ft into South Lake Tahoe, stopped at the California border sign, and reached an Airbnb donated by Nunu's parents.

title: Day 71: Boat day
summary: Rest day in South Lake Tahoe. The team rented a boat, booked by Nunu's family, for tubing, wakeboarding, a cruise through Emerald Bay, and a swim, and returned it by 3 pm.

title: Day 72: GET OFF THE BEACH! THE BEAR IS COMING!
summary: Rest day in South Lake Tahoe. Drew drove about an hour each way to Reno to replace a blown rear tire at a Trek store. Meanwhile the team was dropped at Sand Beach State Park, where a ranger enforced a no-drop-off zone, a bear walked past an open dumpster, and the group split up without phones. The team cooked a last dinner together, and Drew got second-degree burns from frying burgers in hot oil.

title: Day 73: Burn Baby Burn
summary: Rode 100.5 mi from South Lake Tahoe to Folsom, CA, starting with a climb and then an ~8,000 ft descent through a burned forest. Road construction holds, aggressive drivers on the descent, and a bonk from not eating enough made it a hard day; the team reunited for dinner in Folsom with family friends and former Spokes rider Rebecca Lizarde.

title: Day 74: One Last Century of Sidequesting
summary: Rode 108.1 mi from Folsom to Benicia, CA, planned with about ten side quests but stretched to 18 hours. Headwinds and crosswinds across the Sacramento Valley, closed rest stops, dark and freezing riding, and a sushi and IKEA detour delayed the group, who reached their host at 3:20 AM.

title: 2025 Training Plan
summary: A 16-week cycling training plan (from the 2025 team, kept in the 2026 folder) for students with limited time: base, build, peak, taper phases with indoor/outdoor rides, mobility and strength; aims to prepare for the first weeks of multi-day riding rather than full 50-70 mile days.

title: 2026 Training Plan
summary: Short outline of the 2026 training approach: road/indoor/gravel rides, strength (upper, core, lower), and group rides with MIT cycling club plus the Midnight Marathon.

title: Emails (Edgerton correspondence)
summary: Jan 2026 email drafts to Edgerton (Marvelin, Sandra, Chris) covering fundraising logistics, crowdfunding questions, pro/travel cardholders, MVR background checks and car-rental driver list; shows the onboarding steps the finance/fundraising leads must take.

title: Bike Tune-up Raffle

title: Hello!
summary: Placeholder launch post saying the 2025 website was still under construction and linking last year's site.

title: Day -18: First Learning Festival 🥳
summary: Four weeks before departure, the team test-ran two learning festival workshops (Bottle Rocket and Phases of Matter) for students at Carbone Hall in Framingham, MA. The rocket did not lift off, and the food dye was too strong.

title: Day 0: RAHHHH!! SPOKES!! DC!!
summary: Charles and Ruth picked up the team's 2024 Chrysler Pacifica (named Amy), loaded roof and bike racks, and drove from Boston toward DC, lunching with Spokes 2017 alum Caity in Philly. The rest of the team gathered in DC for a kickoff dinner.

title: OFFICIALLY DAY 1 (crazy ik, we're in natural numbers now)
summary: Team ran learning festivals at a DC Department of Corrections facility and at the Youth Services Center, then did errands in the city. Night was spent packing and setting up bikes.

title:
day 2: taking off the training wheels (and lessons learned along the way)
🚴🏼‍♀️
summary: First riding day: DC area to Linden, VA (82 miles, 5,361 ft) over gravel roads, flats, and steep hills. A thunderstorm hit near the host, and the van had to shuttle stranded riders in.

title: Day 3: BLUE RIDGE MOUNTAINS, SHENENDOAH RIVERRRR
summary: Linden, VA to Big Meadows Campground (55.75 miles, 6,555 ft). Riders climbed about 10 miles and 3,000 ft into Shenandoah National Park in heat, and the group reached the campground at sunset.

title: Day 4: thunderstruck⚡️
summary: Big Meadows to Afton, VA (42.74 miles, 3,045 ft). Fog, blind curves, and heavy rain made the Skyline Drive descent unsafe, so riders and bikes were shuttled down by car, and the team reached the host by about 5 pm.

title: Day 5: Can we take five?
summary: Rest day at Pam's property in Afton, VA. The team dried soaked camping gear and cleaned bikes, then went to Charlottesville for laundry, a bike shop repair of broken spokes, and a coffee-shop work session. They also spent hours arguing over the next day's route.

title: Day 6: stab your friends…
summary: Afton to Lexington, VA (47 miles, 4,354 ft). The route included the steepest climb of the trip, averaging 10% with a maximum of 17%. The team reached a Warmshowers host by 3:30 pm.

title: Day 7: The Lone Star Adapts
summary: Lexington to Roanoke, VA (59.6 miles, 4,160 ft). Riders split up and rode at their own pace, and one rider missed the first rest stop. The hosts took the team sightseeing to Roanoke's large star after arrival.

title: Day 8: A Day in the Life (Driver Edition)
summary: Roanoke to Radford, VA (52.4 miles, 4,265 ft), written by the driver. It covers the daily driver role, a failed scratch-off stop, a cooler with unloaded cans, a tuna can with no opener, and dinner and s'mores with the host in Radford.

title: Day 9: forever long miles and the perfect refuel spot
summary: Radford to Tazewell, VA (68.2 miles, 4,380 ft). The day felt long and hot, and a podcast got one rider through the slow middle miles. The team stopped for ice cream and reached the church host in Tazewell.

title: day 10: be my baby 🐣
summary: Learning festival day at Main Street United Methodist Church in Tazewell, VA, with four age groups from kindergarten through high school. Sarah and Joseph were floaters and ran the bottle rocket demo for church members and kids at lunch. Laundry and an ice cream treat followed.

title: Day 11: The Crucible
summary: Tazewell, VA toward Breaks Interstate Park. A rain storm hit at the Honaker Community Center, and the team split on whether to stay there. Ishaq's front derailleur broke, and he finished on a bike with only the big ring. The campsite was the wrong one, and a ranger said it was fine.

title: Day 12: katch me in kentucky
summary: Riders crossed from Virginia into eastern Kentucky on a rainy, rural day. The team went around for rose, thorn, and bud reflections. Saddle sores and unleashed dogs came up often.

title: Day 13: Hazardous Challenges
summary: Learning festival day at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard, KY. Sarah had an allergy scare and took Benadryl, so Joseph ran bottle rockets alone. Ishaq drove two hours to fix his bike, and Tian ran machine learning alone.

title: Day 14: through the fairy forest
summary: Hazard, KY to London, KY (70.7 miles, 5,293 ft) on single-lane backroads through a humid forest. A flooded road forced a reroute onto Hell for Certain Rd (Sizerock), and riders arrived in a thunderstorm at golden hour.

title: Day 15: Choose Your Battles
summary: Tian had a rough day in heat with dizziness and could not finish the route, so she rode in the van for the last 30 miles. There was a near-miss at a stop sign with a car. The team ate a group dinner at Liberty Assembly of God Church.

title: Day 16: Kentucky Fried Chicken
summary: Liberty, KY to Mammoth Cave National Park (88.6 miles, 5,465 ft), the longest ride so far. Ruth was sick and rode in the van. Riders bought a bucket of Lee's Famous Chicken at a rest stop, a bike shop traded a pump for free, and the team had a campfire dinner at the Mammoth Cave campground.

title: Day 17: BUC-EES
summary: Short day from Mammoth Cave to Bowling Green (32.7 miles, 1,342 ft). The team took a self-guided Mammoth Cave tour, rode to the Buc-ee's rest stop in Smith's Grove, KY, then rode the last 17 miles into Bowling Green in rain.

title: day 18: rolling in (bowling) green 💸
summary: Rest day in Bowling Green, KY. The team had breakfast at the Airbnb, Sarah worked from Spencer's Coffee, and everyone cooked burrito night at the house. Sarah reflected on the first 20 days.

title: Day 19: Festive Learning
summary: Bowling Green learning festival day. The machine learning lesson went well: kids built data sets to train a 'happiness detector', and the team tested new extensions to the lesson.

title: Day 20: it's getting hot in here
summary: Bowling Green, KY to Madisonville, KY (84.8 miles, 4,439 ft) in a heat wave with temperatures in the high 90s before noon. The team hosted two WKU students they met at the Bowling Green learning festival for dinner, and stayed at Life Christian Center.

title: Day 21: The highest highs and the lowest lows
summary: Madisonville, KY to Harrisburg, IL (90.3 miles, 2,533 ft). Joseph had heat exhaustion and back pain and got in the van at a rest stop, then rode the last segment with Tian. The route crossed the Ohio River on the Shawneetown Bridge into Illinois, and the team was hosted by Sherry in Harrisburg.

title: Day 22: sweet tea solves everything
summary: Harrisburg, IL to Murphysboro, IL (51.6 miles, 1,314 ft), driven by Ruth. Tian crashed on a gravel turn, and Sarah cleaned her wounds with the first-aid kit. Ruth drove an hour back to Harrisburg for a forgotten bike bib, which was picked up at a Walmart Supercenter.

title: day 23: remember me for…💯
summary: First 100-mile century, Murphysboro IL to St. Louis MO (101.4 mi, 2,540 ft), started at 7:30am from a Warmshowers host. Tian had crashed on gravel the previous day and rode in the car; the team extended its stay in St. Louis by a day.

title: Day 24: every day i'm huSTLin
summary: Rest day in St. Louis: farmers market at Tower Grove Park, the free St. Louis Zoo, and bike maintenance back at the host's house.

title: Day 25: with(out) the sun - light rain and heavy legs
summary: Long Katy Trail day in light rain from St. Louis to Jefferson City MO (125.1 mi, 3,840 ft as listed); riders went self-supported for about 50 miles before the support car shuttled ahead to cut mileage. The gravel went soft and muddy in the rain.

title: Day 26: Best Driver Ever
summary: Driving day from Jefferson City to Sedalia MO (69 mi, 3,250 ft): supermarket runs, a minor van accident in a parking lot, a rider-to-rider crash that left Charles and Greta with cuts and bruises, and a church sleepover.

title: Day 27: Missouri Business
summary: Chill Katy Trail century from Sedalia MO to Kansas City MO, with the riders playing Mr. White on the trail; two falls happened, Ishaq slipping into the bushes and Charles clipping a metal post and hitting his head.

title: Day 28: it takes a(STEAM) village
summary: Learning festival at aSTEAM Village, the finale of a 3.5-week STEM camp (intro to machine learning and phases of matter), followed by a sponsor-hosted dinner with Kansas City community leaders.

title: Day 29: Grand Theft Auto
summary: Kansas City rest day: a visit to The Children's Place (a trauma treatment center for young children), then a rental-car crisis when the recalled Pacifica's contract could not be renewed, so the team kept the van on an overdue contract. Movie night followed.

title: Day 30: And the rockets’ red glare
summary: Kansas City MO to Overbrook KS (77.6 mi, 3,363 ft) on July 4th: Ruth rode 2.5 miles in the wrong direction after a reroute, and at a rest stop at a glass-blowing shop, a rider peering into the windows led to a sheriff visit. Ishaq vomited after rationing water and then chugging drinks at a rest stop.

title: Day 31: Second Fourth of July
summary: Overbrook KS to Emporia KS (61.9 mi, 1,602 ft) on a Kansas day with about a 20 mph headwind; the team visited Scott's retirement community in the morning, got lost on a closed trail, and then had a second Fourth of July at Didde Catholic Center.

title: Day 32: Life is a Highway 🎶
summary: Emporia KS to Newton KS (76.3 mi, 1,602 ft) on US-50: flat, with wide shoulders and no climbs but no shade. Greta snapped a rear derailleur cable and had a nosebleed; the team stayed with hosts Janet and Orvin in Newton.

title: Day 33: Decyphering Newton
summary: Rest-of-trip learning festival day at Newton Public Library, running Ramona's Caesar cipher workshop with small groups, while Tian and Ishaq went to Wichita KS for gloves and a lost glove was recovered from the highway.

title: day 34: fruits and roots 🍎
summary: Newton KS to Macksville KS (92.6 mi, 1,120 ft) in five legs with frequent rest stops; the route included two miles of loose, slippery dirt with close calls but no falls, and the team stayed at Macksville Christian Church.

title: Day 35: Last One Out of Dodge City
summary: Driver blog: Macksville KS to Dodge City KS. The team left at 8:10 after a 6:30 wake-up, lost Joseph's glasses (about 30 minutes of searching), and spent the afternoon at a local water park before a host dinner.

title: Day 36: a picture is worth a thousand words
summary: Photo-only post (no narrative) for Dodge City KS to Lakin KS (79.1 mi, 1,436 ft).

title: Day 37: Centennial Sunflowers
summary: Lakin KS to Lamar CO (77.25 mi, 1,490 ft): crossed into Mountain Time and Colorado, passed the Amache Internment Camp ruins from a distance, and ended with a church community dinner in Lamar. Joseph also outlined the post-trip van drive from San Francisco to Boston.

title: Day 38: screw it
summary: Lamar CO to Fowler CO (86.3 mi, 1,542 ft): Charles's tubeless tire was punctured by a screw and a plug kit burst at 45 PSI, so he rode in the van; the team showered at the pastor's home in Fowler.

title: Day 39: Why did the Chucken Cross the Road?
summary: Fowler CO to Colorado Springs CO (99.7 mi, 4,127 ft), a solo day for Tian: a closed trail for bridge construction, a 75 mph I-25 stretch, a closed rest stop, and detours to avoid gravel. Sarah took her first fall on a steep gravel descent.

title: Day 40: Summertime in the Springs
summary: Colorado Springs rest day: Garden of the Gods, a bike-shop tire replacement and Ace Hardware pliers, and a tire re-mount at the hosts' house. Greta's grandmother was briefly hospitalized after a fall, with no broken bones.

title: Day 41: The Mile High Club
summary: Colorado Springs to Denver CO (66.4 mi, 2,974 ft) on mostly trails (New Santa Fe, Greenland, Plum Creek, Daniels Park). A route road that did not exist sent some riders off-road; a Daniels Park climb and a lake rest stop with a swim were highlights.

title: day 42: adiós, amy! 🚗
summary: Denver learning festival at KIPP Sunshine Peak Academy with rocket launches, followed by an MIT alumni taco dinner in Denver. The team's Enterprise van (Amy) was replaced by an identical silver hybrid.

title: Day 43: Maybe my heart just aint in this 🤷🏾‍♂️
Day 45: What a Wonderful World
summary: Black Hawk CO to Frisco CO (69.75 mi, 7,848 ft): the team crossed Loveland Pass (the trip's highest point), descended the steep dirt Virginia Canyon Road, and finished on the Dillon Reservoir trail after dark.

title: Day 46: good things come to those who wait
summary: Frisco CO to Glenwood Springs CO (93.9 mi, 3,266 ft) through Vail Village (cornhole at the rest stop), desert-like terrain, and a Colorado River swim attempt that failed because the current was too fast. Ishaq's birthday cake plan was set up.

title: Day 47: Birdie needs Sleep.
summary: Learning festival day at Garfield County Public Library in Glenwood Springs, including a machine-learning workshop Tian and Ishaq built over seven festivals. The team also celebrated Ishaq's 22nd birthday and went to the river.

title: Day 48: Which Spokie Are You?
summary: Glenwood Springs CO to Vega State Park CO (56.6 mi, 4,887 ft): a free hot springs stop, a gravel climb between rest stops 2 and 3, and a lakeside campsite where the team cooked grilled cheese and played cards.

title: Day 49: seeya, rockies!
summary: Rode 60.9 miles from Vega State Park down to Grand Junction, CO, leaving the Rockies. A steep unofficial gravel shortcut off I-70 took about 20 minutes to push up, and the team swam in the Colorado River before hosts Greg and Steph fed them.

title: day 50: meet the schmitts 💃🏼
summary: Rode 114.1 miles from Grand Junction, CO to Moab, UT, the second-longest day of the trip, through heat, headwinds, and I-70 with no services for 40-50 miles. A rider's tire trouble created an unofficial rest stop, and the team arrived in Moab after 8:45pm.

title: Day 51: We Gettin Schmittyyyyyy
summary: Rest day in Moab hosted by Sarah's parents: cinnamon rolls, a bike shop and bookstore run, a Colorado River rafting trip, a sunset hike to Delicate Arch in Arches National Park, and a group dinner at an Italian restaurant.

title: Day 52: candyland?? canyonlands!
summary: Second Moab rest day: a six-mile out-and-back hike to The Needles viewpoint in Canyonlands in midday heat, then a hot tub and cornhole night at the condo complex. The hike was harder than the team expected.

title: Day 53: Mother of All Bicycles
summary: Left Moab after a disorganized morning and a fire sandwich stop. Ramona's rear derailleur cable snapped at rest stop 2, so the driver took her to a Moab bike shop and then drove to the Green River campground after the riders arrived.

title: Day 54: we might be on mars
summary: Rode 94.4 miles from Green River State Park to Capitol Reef National Park, with ten climbs, heat, and dehydration. The team arrived at the campground just in time for a $25-per-person dinner, and raccoons stole the bagels from camp that night.

title: Day 55: Entering Dark Sky Zone
summary: Capitol Reef rest day: the team worked from the visitor center Wi-Fi, ran errands, took a scenic drive, and saw very dense stars at the campground. The national park grocery was expensive, and the sunset hike missed the sunset.

title: Day 56: The Seasons of Spokes
summary: Charles drove a long day after packing the campsite alone, which made him miss rest stop 1 and pick up Tian, who could not finish the climb. Headwinds, wildfire smoke, a long gravel ascent, and a bumpy gravel descent left riders exhausted, and the team reached a pastor's house in Escalante after dusk.

title: Day 57: a nice day to Bryce
summary: Rode 51.5 miles from Escalante to Bryce Canyon National Park over two climbs, a viewpoint, and a cafe stop, arriving before dark. A fire ban began at midnight at the campground, so the team had dinner and a fire first.

title: day 58: running it back 🏜️
summary: Bryce Canyon rest day: a hike on the Navajo Loop with steep grades near the end, followed by camp lunch and a group dinner of Ramona's soup and potstickers. The camp restaurant was too expensive and the pizzeria had a long wait.

title: Day 60: maybe paradise is a laundromat in utah
summary: Zion rest day: a team hike up Angels Landing using the shuttle and a permit, with lunch on top and a wade in the river. The Zion laundromat was closed, so the team drove about 20 miles to a Hurricane, UT laundromat late at night.

title: Day 61: The Legendary Metal Dorito
summary: The shortest mileage day (29.75 miles) but the largest single climb of the trip, up Kolob Terrace Road to Lava Point Campground. A sharp piece of metal on the road slashed Ishaq's new tire, and the team washed in cold, muddy Kolob Reservoir because the campground had no showers.

title: Day 62: Elapsed Time Warriors
summary: Rode 89.5 miles from Lava Point to Milford, UT. Tian was badly hurt in a fall on a gravel descent, and the team used phone screenshots for navigation because the route had not been loaded before the campground, which had no service.

title: Day 63: Personal Reckoning
summary: Tian, still recovering from a gravel-descent fall, rode as a passenger while the team rode 83.4 miles from Milford, UT to Baker, NV. Cross-winds made one rider take an hour to cover 7 miles, and the team stayed at a Baker church with no kitchen and a clogged bathroom.

title: Day 64: The One Where We Almost Lose Sarah
summary: Sarah had a serious allergic reaction after eating a muffin made with almond flour at a Baker, NV cafe; Greta gave her an EpiPen, and she was driven to urgent care about 45 minutes away. The rest of the team rode 61.7 miles on Highway 50 to Ely, NV and stayed at a high school.

title: Day 65: the late night zoomies club
summary: Learning festival day in Ely, NV at the library across from the middle school, with about 12 kids and one retired special-education teacher who observed. The afternoon was spent on 3D print troubleshooting and a team dinner at the high school.

title: day 66: home means the hills ⛰️
summary: Rode 69.8 miles along Highway 50 from Ely to Eureka, NV over Robinson Pass (7,607 ft) and several summits. The team shuttled 18 miles north to Diamond Valley Baptist Church, and the car nearly ran out of gas on the way.

title: Day 69: Highway to the Danger Zone
summary: The last learning festival, in Fallon, NV, ran for 6 to 8 kids per group, the team's tenth time running it. A soda bottle with baking soda and vinegar cracked and sprayed a student, and the team slept on a Youth Center teen room couch.

title: Day 70: hey what's up hello
summary: Ruth drove the day, using a spray bottle to wake riders and setting up a float station with ice cream and soda at a rest stop. The team rode 96.8 miles from Fallon, NV to South Lake Tahoe, CA, entered California, and stayed with Warmshowers hosts after dark.

title: Day 72: The Dilly Dally Club Strikes Again
summary: Rode 88.8 miles from South Lake Tahoe to Placerville, CA with about 6,700 ft of climbing and 11,000 ft of descent. The driver brought groceries, fruit, and smoothies, and a one-lane highway closure for log trucks held riders for about 20 minutes near the top.

title: Day 71: Resting is for Winners
summary: South Lake Tahoe rest day: a 28-hole mini golf round that took about four hours, then a beach rock concert with bike valet and a late bowling plan. Food prices at the beach were high.

title: Day 73: Side Questing to the Extreme
summary: A team scavenger hunt with side quests turned a 54.2-mile ride from Placerville into a long day: the first rest stop, 19.4 miles out, came about five hours after the start. The team swam at a park lake and reached Ray and Judy's home in Sacramento in the evening.

title: day 74: choose your own adventure 🗺️
summary: The team split into a Six Flags group that left early and a regular group that rode 74.9 miles from Sacramento to Benicia, CA through Davis, Dixon, and Vacaville. They rode the last stretch after dark on an interstate service road and arrived at 10:30pm.

title: Day 77: Spokes 2025 final season series FINALE, the real, true end
summary: Final San Francisco day: the team packed the van one last time, then toured Ghirardelli Square and Japantown and ate a Thai dinner, the team's final supper. Greta left at 6am for a flight, and the rest rode autonomous taxis back to the house.

title: Day 78: is it all over?
summary: After the team's flights left in the morning, the last three riders drove 426 miles north along the coast, stopping at Humboldt Redwoods, a Pacific beach, and Redwoods National Park. They arrived at Humbug Mountain State Park, OR after dark.

title: Day 79: Dilly Dallying One Last Time
summary: Drove the Oregon coast (Hwy 101) from Humbug Mountain State Park to Seattle, stopping at a near-empty beach, Sea Lion Caves, Thor's Well, Cape Kiwanda and Tillamook. A bike-rack hit on a parked car and a 1.5-hour advisor call delay pushed them into Seattle after midnight.

title: Day 80: blue lakes, orange berries and the skies above us
summary: Left Seattle and drove through North Cascades National Park (Gorge Creek Falls, a cold Diablo Lake swim, rowan berries), with a van gas-door problem and a failed propane stove along the way. They camped by Curlew Lake State Park in Washington.

title: Day 81: Glacial Troubles
summary: Woke up very cold at Curlew Lake, WA, then fought a van fuel-fill problem, a dirty windshield, and the stove failure. They drove up Going-to-the-Sun Road to Logan Pass, where a couple offered help, and reached Duck Lake, MT after dark.

title: Day 82: Ancient Lands, Empty yet Grand
summary: Drove from Duck Lake, MT through Browning and Helena, losing over two hours in Helena to failed stove troubleshooting before buying a working propane canister. They then rushed through Yellowstone to Old Faithful and reached Lizard Creek Campground in Grand Teton National Park after dark.

title: Day 83: The Desolate Heartland
summary: The longest drive of the trip so far (560 mi): from Lizard Creek, WY through Dubois, the Wind River foothills, Thunder Basin, Wright and Mount Rushmore to a dirt road into Sage Creek Campground in the Badlands, SD after dark.

title: Day 84: Safari in the Badlands
summary: Bison and prairie dogs at Sage Creek Campground in the morning, then a Badlands drive and a long I-90 stretch east. They ended the day at a host family's house in Madison Lake, MN after Google Maps routed them onto a closed, muddy road.

title: [Sponge-talk] Spokes 2025 x List Visual Arts Center Bike by Public Art
summary: Spokes 2025 partnered with MIT List Visual Arts Center on a free biking tour of MIT public art (meet Ames and Main BlueBikes station, Sun Apr 27 2025 2pm), used to promote the S25 crowdfunding page. Postponed to Sun May 4 2025 for weather.

title: Day -96: Welcome to Spokes 2024!
summary: Pre-trip intro post: Rebecca introduces herself and the eight-member 2024 team, who are route planning, fundraising, and setting up learning festivals before the summer ride.

title: What Spokes Did Over Spring Break
summary: Team members recount their spring break trips: a lithium policy research trip in Arkansas, a yurt stay in Vermont, a Finger Lakes AirBnB, a Peru trek, a Montreal trip, a Natchez Trace ride in Mississippi, and a Saranac Lake stay.

title: Day 1: Spokes' First Learning Festival!
summary: Days -1 and 0 were spent driving and prepping near DC. Day 1 was the first learning festival, split between the DC Jail (adults over 18) and the DC Youth Services Center, teaching concrete chemistry (Krispie Koncrete), strawberry DNA, a 3D-printed boat, and Scratch coding.

title: Day 2: First Day on the Road - Scenic Views in Virginia, Chaos, Tacos, and More Chaos
summary: First riding day, Oakton VA to Linden VA: several falls (Hank, Jess on a gravel road), a bike breakdown that needed a van pickup, and the discovery that the rental minivan had bald front tires, which forced a rest day.

title: Day 3: A Necessary Res(e)t Day
summary: Rest day in Linden VA: two riders tried to get a new rental car at Dulles after the bald-tire discovery, which took three rentals and an Uber ride. The team also got bikes checked and fitted in Winchester VA and cooked dinner together.

title: Day 5: Sweet Tea, Baby
summary: Shenandoah National Park (Big Meadows camp) to Waynesboro VA: a fast downhill out of the park, lunch at Lil Gus's in Grottoes, then a long detour to add all riders as authorized drivers on the rental car at an Avis 45 minutes away, where only four additional drivers could be added.

title: Day 6: Virginia is for Lovers
summary: Flat ride from Waynesboro to Lexington VA (43.8 mi), where riders reflected on adjusting to 8-hour riding days, then spent the afternoon kayaking and paddleboarding with Warmshowers hosts Dirk and Chrissy.

title: Day 4: Parallel Universes on the Spokes Team
summary: Note: this file is the Day 4 post (title and date say Day 4 and 2024-06-10; the filename says day-6). Linden VA to Shenandoah NP: a 60.9-mile, 7,569 ft day where the support van's hybrid rental failed on Skyline Drive, leaving the support crew stranded for hours until a tow, a replacement rental, and a truck to move camping gear were arranged. Riders reached Big Meadows Campground after dark.

title: Day 7: Planks on Plank
summary: Lexington to Roanoke VA (58.6 mi): a water stop on Plank Road, lunch at a Buchanan picnic area, a closed bike path detoured onto a highway for 20 miles, and a Roanoke bridge demolition that forced a detour before reaching hosts Howard and Lynn.

title: Day 10: Flat Tires and Hilly Roads
summary: Tazewell VA to Breaks Interstate Park (70.9 mi, 5,851 ft): a flat on Cleo's tire that could not be fixed roadside because the team had no pump and the tire was not actually tubeless; the van had to return to help, and the team camped at the VA/KY border.

title: Day 11: A Break in Breaks
summary: Rest day at Breaks Interstate Park: the team napped in hammocks, one rider got a flat fixed at a local bike shop while the car was used, and the group ate at the Rhododendron Restaurant. Tents in the open field got very hot by morning.

title: Day 9: You Gotta Do It Everyday
summary: Draper VA to Tazewell VA (69.1 mi, 4,701 ft): a rider pushed through shin-splint pain on the team's longest ride so far, with a steep downhill in the first 25 miles and a night at Main Street Methodist Church in Tazewell.

title: Day 8: 🎵 On The Road Again 🎵
summary: Roanoke VA to Draper VA (60.9 mi): after closed routes forced a reroute, the team lunched in Christiansburg and reached a Warmshowers winery property in Draper, where they toured the vines and ate pizza outside.

title: Day 12: Who let the dogs (and other animals) out??
summary: Breaks Interstate Park to Hazard KY (77.9 mi, 4,255 ft): the team was chased by dogs, including one that caused a crash into bushes, and rode past a coal-history mural and a dairy bar before reaching a Hazard B&B.

title: Day 13: Spokes Goes to Space Camp
summary: Second learning festival at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard KY, with Krispie Koncrete, physics of sound speakers, 3D-printed bubble wands, and strawberry DNA. The afternoon was spent in town at Hazard Coffee Co., the Mother Goose Inn, and the Perry County fair.

title: Day 14: Concerning the Kentucky Leash Ban
summary: Hazard KY to Koomer Ridge (70.8 mi, 4,211 ft): dogs chased riders through unleashed-dog Kentucky, mid-90s afternoon heat, and a pothole on a gravel road caused a fall; closed roads forced a 10-mile backroad detour.

title: Day 15: Bikin' and Bourbon
summary: Red River Gorge campground to Lexington KY (64.3 mi, 2,702 ft): the team started at 5 am to beat heat, bought distillery tour tickets during a long Dairy Queen stop, and were hosted by Ken and Tricia in Lexington.

title: Day 16: memes and nicknames
summary: Lexington KY to Liberty KY (69.3 mi): a cafe lunch in Danville, team nicknames, meme-making after arrival at 2 pm, and an overnight at a church in Liberty; one rider got sick from the team's food and cooler.

title: Day 17: New time zone and CAVES!!!
summary: Liberty KY to Mammoth Cave National Park (83.08 mi, 3,698 ft): a reroute took riders down a dead-end dirt road and then onto gravel; the team crossed into Central time and took the Discovery Tour at Mammoth Cave with Ranger Brendan.

title: Day 18: Longest Day of the Year!
summary: Short 32-mile ride from Mammoth Cave to Bowling Green KY after a rider finally got 8+ hours of sleep. The team worked from Spencer's Cafe, toured a music and thrift store, and stayed in a house arranged by the learning-festival partner.

title: Day 19: Bowling Green Learning Festival
summary: Largest learning festival so far at Accelerate KY in Bowling Green (50-60 middle schoolers): physics demos, Krispie Koncrete, strawberry DNA, 3D printing, and speaker building, which got local TV coverage. Several riders then got a stomach bug.

title: Day 20: Bushwhacking and Gravel Riding
summary: Bowling Green KY to Madisonville KY (85.4 mi, 4,063 ft): a GPS route sent riders onto a gravel forest road that two riders bushwhacked through with bikes, then they jumped a divider to ride the state highway shoulder. Hank's parents supported the team with water and electrolytes.

title: Day 21: A Day on 4 Wheels
summary: Driver's-day post: Madisonville KY to Harrisburg IL (82.27 mi). A thunderstorm delayed packing and the team camera had to be rescued, a rider's chain was stuck and the bike was driven back after the toolbox was left behind, and the van crossed into Illinois. The driver team hosted with Sherie and Brad.

title: Day 22: It's Worth It, the Sunsets
summary: Short 43-mile ride from Harrisburg IL to Gun Creek Campground: the team spent the morning in Benton IL at a coffee shop, an antique shop, and the library, then swam in the lake at Gun Creek and prepared for a 104-degree century ride the next day.

title: Day 23: 💯
summary: Gun Creek Campground IL to St Louis MO (107 mi, 2,180 ft) in 100-plus-degree heat: riders started at 4:30 am, drafted in pairs for the first half, and one rider ran low on water at mile 60 before a homeowner refilled bottles; the team finished the century at 102 degrees and had dinner with an MIT alum.

title: Day 24: A Rest Day in Saint Louis
summary: Rest day in St. Louis: one rider walked about two hours to the Gateway Arch, the team bought the national park sticker there, and they had dinner with hosts and their friends.

title: Day 25: No More Cars
summary: Rode 83 miles from St. Louis suburbs onto the Katy Trail and ended at a treehouse in Hermann, MO; the rider ran out of food by mile 35 and arrived late.

title: Day 26: Am I Dreaming?
summary: Easy 51-mile Katy Trail ride from Hermann to Jefferson City; the team had bike fit checks at a local shop, cooked Japanese curry for the host, and went to the host's brewery gig.

title: Day 27: 41 Million Revolutions
summary: Rode 60 miles from Jefferson City to Sedalia, MO in a flat, low-morale slog; the team had a famous barbecue lunch at Kehde's and slept in Antioch church with only a hose for showers.

title: Day 28: We have the Tour de France at home (jk)
summary: First century (118.85 miles) from Sedalia, MO to Osawatomie, KS, taking 13 hours; branches on the Katy Trail damaged derailleurs, and hosts Jeff and Sarah fit bikes and taught maintenance.

title: Day 29: Pick Your Poison
summary: Riders were caught in a severe thunderstorm on the Flint Hills Trail and then KS-68 (no shoulder, heavy semis), took refuge in a cafe, and added a 10-mile gravel detour around a flooded trail to reach Council Grove, KS.

title: Day 30: Kansas Entrance Exam
summary: Rode 73 miles from Council Grove to Newton, KS into a 20 mph headwind and 110 F heat index, then a lightning storm with 60-70 mph gusts near Walton; three riders took refuge in a ditch and a host van picked them up.

title: Day 31: Castles, Bubble Wands, and Everything in Between
summary: Ran a learning festival at the Newton Public Library with Tinkercad bubble-wand design and 3D printing, strawberry DNA extraction, and physics demos; the team then had ice cream at Braum's and pizza with their hosts.

title: Day 32: 'MURICA 🦅🦅🦅
summary: Rode US-50 across the Kansas prairie and celebrated July 4 with hot dogs and sparklers; the planned Stafford RV Park was swapped for a legal stealth camp at the Highway 50 rest area.

title: Day 33: Viva la Vida
summary: Flat 76-mile US-50 ride from Stafford to Dodge City, KS through a 17-mile wind farm; a rider got a first flat that was fixed roadside with a hand pump, and the team visited Paleteria La Michoacana and Boot Hill Museum.

title: Day 34: Which MIT Spokes member are you?
summary: A driving day for the van: the driver helped a rider fix a flat, bought lunch and supplies in Garden City, and had pizza at Victory Baptist Church; the post is mostly a personality quiz.

title: Day 35: "I don't think we're in Kansas anymore."
summary: Rode 78 miles from Lakin, KS to Lamar, CO through a rain shower and crossed into Colorado; one rider toured a large Kansas dairy farm in the morning, and the team cooked a dinner in a bar's industrial kitchen after sleeping in a motel converted to dorms.

title: Day 36: When we’re big kids
summary: Lamar, CO rest day: the team ran a strawberry DNA learning festival on the library patio, then went to Pike's Tower and a park, and ate Indian food in the motel parking lot.

title: Day 37: Junk in our Trunk -- What I Packed for Spokes
summary: Hot, flat, dry 86-mile ride from Lamar to Fowler, CO with few services; the post is a team packing-list review and a donation request for gear.

title: Day 38: It's Jolene's World, and We're All Just Living in It
summary: Rode 99.76 miles from Fowler to Colorado Springs over desolate, hot terrain; one rider showed early heat stroke symptoms, and the team had dinner with an MIT alum and went to a college rodeo.

title: Day 39: We're not in Kansas Anymore 2
summary: Rode 61 miles from Colorado Springs to Denver on bike-friendly roads; the rider's father met them on the road, and the host David offered bike safety checks while the rider hunted for brake pads.

title: Day 41: Mother Infrastructure
summary: Tried to ride US-285 out of Denver and then a ten-mile Conifer climb; the 285 was too scary (one rider nearly hit by a truck on a downhill), so five riders shuttled to the Kenosha Campground, CO (the post lists 44.8 miles and 4,196 ft ridden against 74.6 miles and 7,556 ft planned).

title: Day 40: Denver Rest Day :)
summary: Denver rest day: moved from one host's house to another, visited Spokes alum Kate, shopped at REI, toured Red Rocks (closed for a concert), and explored RiNO with a local friend.

title: Day 42: Reckoning with Mortality
summary: Ride from Kenosha Campground to Buena Vista, CO (65.3 miles): gravel on Elkhorn Road was too loose so the riders turned back, the US-285 descents were terrifying, and after a flat fix and a wait at the CO-9 junction the group kept riding the 285 to Buena Vista.

title: Day 43: "I think my life might be better if I lived in Colorado (mmm)"
summary: Buena Vista rest day: hiked Harvard Lakes in the Collegiate Range, swam in the cold lake, met Stanford Spokes for dinner in Salida, and returned to find tents blown over in a storm on the host's lawn.

title: Day 44: Spokes vs the Continental Divide
summary: Rode 68.6 miles from Buena Vista to Gunnison, CO over a 20-mile continuous climb to the Continental Divide, then a fast descent along the Taylor River; hosts Thalia and Jeff cooked dinner.

title: Day 45: A GOATed Day
summary: Gunnison rest day with a learning festival in town: students made concrete sharks and speakers, and the team had breakfast and a backyard dinner with their hosts Thalia and Jeff.

title: Day 46: Call Us James 'cause It’s Getting Peachy
Day 47: What I Eat in a Day
summary: Rode 68.8 miles from Paonia to Grand Junction, CO on a day that was uneventful; the post describes the team's food: bagels, Clif bars, a Wendy's stop in Delta, a salami sandwich lunch, gelato, and a shared dinner.

title: Day 48: Yay Utah
summary: Rode 106 miles (the post lists 106/127) from Grand Junction, CO to Moab, UT along the Colorado River canyons; the border was marked by gravel, three riders had flats within 15 minutes, and one rider had heat exhaustion in the last 10 miles.

title: Day 49: Delicate Knees at Delicate Arch
summary: Rest day in Moab after a 100-mile day with six flats. The team cooled off in the Colorado River, got frozen yogurt, toured Arches, and hiked to Delicate Arch.

title: Day 50: Sunsets and Moonrises
summary: Ran errands in Moab (bike shop, supplies, library), then rode an evening 34-mile route to Wingate Campground and raced sunset without a front light.

title: Day 51: Jackass Joe's
summary: Rode US-91 and I-70 across high desert to Green River, stopping at a novelty 'AREA STUPID' gas station and racing last year's team's Strava times on a tailwind downhill.

title: Day 52: Ah Shit, Here We Go Again
summary: Flats before leaving camp, then the support van got stuck on rough gravel and missed the first water stop, so riders collected 16 water bottles from strangers on the highway. Rode about 100 miles through Hanksville to Capitol Reef and swam in the Fremont River, which later tested above recommended E. coli levels.

title: Day 53: We Can't Read Signs
summary: Rest day at Capitol Reef: a grocery run to a town about 30 minutes away, a cafe and ice cream stop in Torrey, laundry and route planning, and a late hike in which three riders took the Rim Overlook trail by mistake instead of Hickman Bridge.

title: Day 54: Cosmic Gratitude
summary: A long day (78 miles, 7,365 ft) through a national forest, a narrow ridge road, and desert on Utah Scenic Byway 12. Cleo crashed at speed on a steep descent where she had skipped braking, broke her arm, and was out at least four weeks. This was the team's first accident.

title: Day 55: Moo and Hoodoo and Food
summary: An easy 47-mile ride to Bryce Canyon, with a cow race and a town misspelling of Hank's name. The afternoon was a hike among the hoodoos, and the evening was dinner at Bryce Canyon Lodge and stargazing with a family member.

title: Day 57: Diary of a Limpy Kid
summary: A timestamped log of an 80-mile ride from Bryce to Zion, with headwinds on UT-12. At lunch Cleo decided to go home. In Zion the bikes could not go through the Mt. Carmel Tunnel, so Jess shuttled the riders through by van. The team got Angel's Landing permits.

title: Day 56: Look on the Bryce side
summary: Rest day in Bryce. Cleo had fractured her right elbow two days earlier (four-week estimate, no biking), and she weighed staying as a passenger against flying home to France. The team hiked the hoodoos and ate ice cream.

title: Day 58: Angels Landing and Angel’s Departing
summary: Hiked Angel's Landing on a lottery permit. Then the team had a Thai dinner and a farewell dance for Cleo, who left the team the next morning.

title: Day 59: Spokes in the Narrows
summary: Sent Cleo off toward St. George for her bus and plane home. Then hiked The Narrows of the Virgin River from the Zion bus stop, and biked to a Motel 6 in Hurricane with exhausted legs.

title: Day 60: A How-To Guide for Boring Rides
summary: A long, dull 100-mile day from Hurricane to Milford. The route went about 90 miles northeast, away from the West Coast. Riders had flats, a first lunch of Cedar City fast food, a drafting crash, and a team cheesesteak dinner after a night at a church.

title: Day 61: Desert Magic
summary: A hot, empty US-50 ride from Milford into Nevada, with a shoulder lunch and no services. The team crossed into Pacific Time and posed at the Nevada sign. In Baker, pop. 21, they had ice cream and dinner, then a night festival with live music at the general store.

title: Day 62: Senioritis
summary: The Nevada mountain ranges start: about 4,300 ft of climbing on a 'short' 61-mile day to Ely. Barbed wire gashed a rider's hand at the campground, lunch slid to 3 pm, and the team recovered poolside at a motel in Ely.

title: Day 63: We Love Stickers
summary: A sticker-collection recap of the whole trip. The day itself was 50 miles of Nevada wasteland to a shoulder lunch, then 30 more miles to a camp at the county fairground in Eureka. Stops covered include Breaks Interstate Park hammocks, the Osawatomie, KS host, Tallgrass headwinds, JJ Mercantile water on UT-128, and the Baker night market.

title: Day 64: A non-biking day in Portugal
summary: Cleo's non-biking day in Porto, Portugal with her family. The post also includes riders' quotes about their Eureka to Austin, Nevada ride (67.7 mi, 2,943 ft).

title: Day 65: Me and the Flies Against the World
summary: The longest ride of the trip, 112 miles on the Loneliest Road in America (US-50), in 99°F heat and headwinds. The rider went solo until the Middlegate stop at mile 64, then pushed on alone to the Fallon Youth Club for dinner with the host.

title: Day 66: The Oasis of Nevada
summary: A learning festival day at the Fallon Youth Club: Strawberry DNA extraction, a Physics of Sound speaker workshop, and catch-and-run with students. The team also found out about US-50 road work between Fallon and Silver Springs. The detour decision was postponed to the morning.

title: Day 67: One Final Ass Whooping from Nevada
summary: Took the 15-mile detour to avoid Nevada road work, then climbed the Carson Range from about 4,700 to over 7,100 ft. The team descended into California on a shoulderless road. Amulya's dead backlight meant a van pickup after dark.

title: Day 68: The First of Many Lasts
summary: The day after a 15-mile pickup from a dark, shoulderless road. The team rode to the Lake Tahoe STEM Academy at the Boys & Girls Club. The writer taught fourth graders Strawberry DNA, saw a black bear near the field, and watched high school robotics teams test boats.

title: Day 69:  Lifestyle Whiplash
summary: A rest day in South Lake Tahoe: cafe-hopping and work, a call with Cleo, then a lake boat outing and dinner hosted by Marina and Rafael. Hank and JD shipped the learning festival materials back to Boston.

title: Day 70: The Curse Ends
summary: A rest day in Lake Tahoe. Amulya fell off a curb while biking to the resort, hit her head and shoulders, and was treated at a hospital for a minor concussion. The hospital said she could still bike. The team had a lackluster beach visit and cooked congee.

title: Day 71: Bumming Around (Savoring Every Moment)
summary: A 90-mile day over Carson Pass, with a 1,000-ft climb at about 8% and then a long downhill through the Caldor Fire burn area. The team stopped at the Carson Pass visitor center for free watermelon and ate lunch by an alpine lake. They reached a church host in Placerville after getting lost looking for it.

title: Day 72: The Promised Lands — Portugal and Sacramento
summary: Cleo's post covers her family's Portugal trip. Varsha's riders' post covers a flat ride from Placerville to Sacramento along the American River trail, a French bread lunch, Salt and Straw ice cream, dinner with host Bob, and a Chinese buffet.

title: Day 73: 28 Things You Have to Do Before We Both Die
summary: Sacramento to Benicia (72 miles). A non-hitch bike rack fell off the minivan on a speed bump and dragged two bikes. The rack was reattached and the bikes went to a shop. The riders also dealt with detours and flats. The rest of the post is a 28-item to-do list by state.

title: Day 74: THE FINALE
summary: Final riding day from Benicia to San Francisco (42.3 mi, 2,513 ft): the team rode together, crossed three Bay Area bridges and a steep climb after Corte Madera, then reached the Golden Gate finish and spent the afternoon packing and shipping bikes at the San Francisco REI, which stayed open past closing while they finished.

title: Day 75: The REAL Spokes OGs
summary: Rest/logistics day in San Francisco (0 mi): the team finished packing bikes at REI, struggled to ship them cheaply (FedEx and UPS were expensive, and REI boxes were oversized), then had dinner with original Spokes founder Turner and alumni Nathan and Kaitlyn, held a Spokes party, and some riders got matching tattoos of the route.
