title: Our First Learning Festival (in MA)
summary: Spokes ran its first Learning Festival, a pre-departure session at a Massachusetts DYS juvenile justice facility, where four riders taught 3D printing and berry-dye solar cell workshops. Students doubted the team would actually bike across the country.

title: First Day!
summary: Day one: the team left the Lincoln Memorial and rode the East Coast Greenway and busy Virginia roads toward Stafford, VA (about 58 miles planned). Sophia got leg cramps in the heat and rode in the support car for the rest of the day.

title: Day 2: CONTINUED and Day 4: The Lake
summary: Day 2: on Virginia backroads a sudden thunderstorm forced the team to huddle until the Mineral Volunteer Fire Department truck picked them up, and a replacement bike rack was bought from a shop about an hour away. Day 4 was a rest day at a lake, then dumpling night at a host's home in Charlottesville.

title: Belated Day 3: Our First Learning Festival ✨on the road✨
summary: First Learning Festival on the road, at the Louisa County Public Library in Virginia, with 3D printing, music, leaf chromatography, circuits and solar cell workshops. The library coordinator then recommended a soft-serve stop, and the team stayed with a friend of Sophia's in Charlottesville.

title: Day 5: Into the Woods (and up the Mountain)
summary: Left Charlottesville for Loft Mountain Campground in Shenandoah National Park, a 3,717 ft gain. Paved country roads turned into steep gravel and bushes, then a long Skyline Drive climb and a final steep mile, with a driver meeting them at a halfway picnic table.

title: Day 7: We Came, We Saw, We Walked up the Hill
summary: Breakfast with host Pam (grits and biscuits), then 45 miles to Lexington, VA. The team hit very steep climbs for about 10 miles after a ski shop stop, then rode wet switchbacks in rain and a long descent on Bike Route 76 before arriving at Dirk and Chrissie's home.

title: Day 8: Eat, Sleep, Bike
summary: Rode 55 miles from Lexington to Roanoke, VA, on the Chessie Nature Trail (gravel) and Bike Route 76, which avoided the Shenandoah climbs. A storm at the Buchanan Swinging Bridge led to two car shuttle trips, and the team cleaned and lubed their chains in Roanoke.

title: Day 10: Longest Ride So Far!
summary: Longest ride so far at 78 miles, from hosts Curtis and Jennifer through Trans America Trail (US Bike Route 76) signs and roads beside the interstate, with a cemetery lunch, ending in Abingdon, VA at Warmshowers host Julia's home.

title: Day 11: Welcome to the Family
summary: Rode 70 miles from Abingdon to Breaks Interstate Park on the VA/KY border. A lunch stop turned into a free potluck with a Tiller family reunion, and the final approach to the campground was uphill the whole way.

title: Day 12: Taking a Break at Breaks
summary: Rest day at Breaks Interstate Park: visitor center, a 0.35-mile geological hike, and a swim at the Russell Fork River in Kentucky. The team gave water to a lost couple on the trail and had a campfire that night.

title: Day 14: The Ducks of Hazard
summary: Rode 41.7 miles from Wayland, KY to Hazard, KY with no incidents, stopping for a long break on the way. The team stayed with Wayland's mayor and his wife, then slept in a duck-themed room in Hazard.

title: Day 15, 16, 17: Relax, you're in the mountains
summary: Ran two days of workshops at the Hazard, KY Challenger Center (solar cells from berry juice for middle schoolers), plus the county fair. On June 17 they rode to the Red River Gorge area, waited out a thunderstorm in a church awning, and sheltered at a campground when the rain came.

title: Day 18: A Type B- High Energy Type of Day
summary: Rode 68 miles from Red River Gorge to Lexington, KY on a cooler 74 F day after a heat wave. Dogs chased the team, and on the suburban roads into Lexington they witnessed a hit-and-run scene before police arrived. They stayed with church-group hosts Tony and Lynda.

title: Day 19: Fathers, feasts, and the friends we made along the way
summary: Rode 63.79 miles from Lexington to Liberty, KY, with a park lunch of barbacoa burritos and Father's Day calls. Don and Cindy Cravens hosted a big dinner, then their family gave a farm tour, and the night ended with geodes in a fire pit.

title: Day 20: 90 miles and a visit with an old friend
summary: Rode 90 miles from Liberty to the Mammoth Cave campsite in roughly three 30-mile sections, in heat near 95 F. An Amish family fixed a flat on the way, and the team refilled water at gas stations.

title: Day 21: Caves, Cows, Corn, and Corvettes!
summary: Visited Mammoth Cave (55 F inside) and the Corvette Museum in Bowling Green, then rode 30.8 miles on hot farm roads to a hotel in Bowling Green. Berries were bought at a Kroger for the next day's solar cell workshop.

title: Day 22: News Travels Fast and Day 23: We Travel 13.0 mph
summary: Ran the Bowling Green, KY learning festival at WKU's Innovation Campus, which got local TV and newspaper coverage. Then rode 50.7 miles to Hartford, KY, where hosts Sharilyn and Tony had a pool and a bourbon tasting.

title: Day 24: Chicken and Corn. Straight from the source.
summary: Rode 62.9 miles from Hartford to Henderson, KY through corn fields, chicken-farm country and Owensboro's bike paths, with a fried chicken lunch at a nature park. Stayed with hosts Karen and Roy in a cabin in Audubon Park.

title: Day 25: Welcome to the Land of Lincoln!
summary: Rode from Henderson, KY across the Ohio River into Illinois. Lunch at Fiedlerland RV Park in Old Shawneetown, then Warmshowers hosts Sherie and Brad in Harrisburg, who had biked Oregon to Maine the year before, fed the team watermelon and sourdough.

title: Day 26: Baking Brad
summary: Rode 51 miles from Harrisburg to Murphysboro, IL, after waiting out morning thunderstorms and leaving around 2 PM, the latest departure of the trip so far. Stayed with Terry and Linda, Beatles fans with a pool that has a diving board.

title: Day 27: I am in Misery
summary: Rode 44 miles from Murphysboro, IL to Perryville, MO, with a lunch stop in Chester, IL and a crossing of the Mississippi into Missouri. Learned the host lived in a St. Louis suburb, which turned the next day into a 97-mile ride. The team decorated their car with chalk markers.

title: Day 0: Let’s Rewind to our DC Learning Festival
summary: The day before departure, the team ran a Learning Festival at a DC youth rehabilitation center (Maya Angelou Academy, with DYRS and YSC). It was also a scramble: members were still arriving, the bike rack was broken, and driver registration at Budget was still pending.

title: Day 28: St. Louis Blues
summary: Rode 92 miles from Perryville, MO to Chesterfield, MO, a St. Louis suburb, in three sections. A flat from road debris, a gravel road being repaved that forced a walk downhill, and a noisy highway shoulder for the last stretch.

title: Day 29 and Day 30: STL means St. Louis!
summary: Rest day in St. Louis: City Museum, the Arch, the Delmar Loop and Washington University. The next day ran the sixth Learning Festival at a Ferguson middle school summer program (the post says Ferguson, MI, but it is in the St. Louis area), then a potluck with host Noah.

title: Day 34: Fourth of July and Day 35: Our First Century
summary: Fourth of July rest day at Lake of the Ozarks, MO: caving at Ozark Caverns to escape the heat, then a swim at the lake. The next day was the first century, 105 miles from the lake to Springfield, MO (the post says MI). A bumpy gravel road, a broken pump and long rolling hills pushed them to a 9 PM arrival at barber and cyclist Greg's home.

title: Day 36: French Connection
summary: Rode 71.7 miles from Springfield MO to Carthage MO after a flat tire and a road closure where the road segment was missing; a passing driver led them on a short detour. Hosts in Carthage gave them watermelon and a scenic route past the Battle of Carthage site.

title: Day 37: 404 Page Not Found, and Day 38: Lakefront Rest Day
summary: Rode 60 miles from Carthage MO into Kansas, where Google Maps routed them onto several miles of treacherous gravel. Took a rest day at Lake Crawford in Farlington KS after finding a missing day in their route spreadsheet and fixing it.

title: Day 39: Oh Deer
summary: Rider Simone was hit by a deer on Highway 54 in Kansas while riding the protected shoulder with sun glare in her eyes, about 6 miles from a 100-mile goal. She was checked at the local hospital and the team stayed at a church in Eureka KS; she then rested a few days and got a new helmet and pants at REI.

title: Day 40: HALFWAY DONE!!
summary: Reached the halfway point of the 80-day trip. Rode 75 flat miles on US Route 76 (Transamerica) from Eureka KS to Newton KS, where Warm Showers hosts (a Mennonite family) fed them tacos with local corn. A team member walked to a grocery store for berries and black grape juice for the solar-cell workshop.

title: Day 41: Newton Students Knew-Tons More After Our Workshops!
summary: Taught a learning festival at the Newton Public Library in Kansas. Workshops covered color and chromatography and circuits. Then the team drove to Wichita to fix the car window and pick up bikes from a bike shop, but came back without the part needed to finish the bike repair.

title: Day 42: Jesus, Would You Look At the Time
summary: Left Newton KS late after an early-morning Ford dealership visit for the car window. Rode about 92 miles to Great Bend KS on flat, tailwind-assisted roads past tofu bean and sunflower fields. A helmet crack found at lunch sent one rider to the car for the rest of the day.

title: Day 43: The Windy City is... Dodge City, KS
summary: Rode 87.6 miles into a strong headwind from Great Bend to Dodge City KS, past wind farms and grain elevators. The four riders drafted in a tight line about 5 feet apart, rotating the lead every 30 minutes. Dinner was pizza and local beer at the Dodge City Brewery with hosts Lindy and Warren.

title: Day 44: And Then There Were Three
summary: Rode 49.8 miles from Dodge City to Lakin KS with only three riders, shuttling the last 20 miles to a motel to avoid heat and wind. Host Lindy chased the team down to return four water bottles left behind. Lunch was El Salvadoran pupusas in Garden City KS.

title: Day 45: A Whole Lot to Love's
summary: Rode 85 miles from Lakin KS into Colorado, crossing a time zone change, in heat near 102 degrees and a headwind. Dinner was rotisserie chicken and General Tso's chicken at the motel.

title: Day 46 + 47: Car Wash vs DQ Ice Cream
summary: Taught the 8th learning festival at Lamar Public Library in Colorado to a small group of four very engaged kids. The next day rode 81.5 miles from Lamar to Fowler CO, with a Dairy Queen stop at mile 36 when the gas station was closed.

title: Spokes Day 48: Where the Wild Things Are
summary: Rode from Fowler CO into Colorado's foothills; the plains turned to desert and then hills. A thunderstorm forced a car ride for the last part into Colorado Springs. The team met a solo touring cyclist named Caleb and learned Vail Pass (10,662 ft) is ahead.

title: Day 49 and Day 50: Alter-Egos from Another Coast
summary: Rest day in Colorado Springs with a 23-mile morning ride to Garden of the Gods with host Ken. Met the Stanford Spokes team at a Subway in Ellicott CO and got bikes repaired at Ted's Bicycles in Colorado Springs. On July 20 rode 65 miles on the 105 country road to Centennial, CO, with lunch at O'Brien's Cafe in Sedalia.

title: Day 51: A Tale of Two Cities & Day 52: Black Hawk Up
summary: July 21 was a split rest day in Denver. The team replaced a defective rental car window while a friend and the author toured Red Rocks, Lookout Mountain and Meow Wolf. On July 22 the team rode 54 miles from Centennial to Blackhawk CO, climbing 5,353 ft into the mountains, and got a triple rainbow on the way.

title: Day 53: A Break for Our Brakes
summary: Rode 55 miles from Blackhawk to Silverthorne CO and climbed 7,055 ft, including Loveland Pass near 12,000 ft. Cold rain and hail left riders without enough warm layers, and the support car picked them up. A steep gravel descent into Idaho Springs wore out hands and brakes.

title: Day 54: A Magical Day
summary: Rode 90.7 miles from Silverthorne CO to Glenwood Springs, mostly downhill out of the Rockies, including a descent from Vail Pass through Vail. Stayed with Warm Showers host Greg in Glenwood Springs, who performed a card-magic show that evening.

title: Day 56: Cloudy with a chance of fugitive
summary: Sophia took a rest day after 5 hours of sleep. The bikers rode from Rifle CO to a lunch stop in De Beque, where a police activity and a storm interrupted; the support crew shuttled the bikers past an interstate section because it was unsafe after rain. The team ended in Grand Junction CO with host Erika, who made a spaghetti dinner.

title: Day 57: Entering Hatu... or Utah?
summary: Rode 84.6 miles from Grand Junction through Fruita on separated bike paths, then into desert on gravel after the Utah line. Stopped in Cisco UT, a ghost town with an artist community. Camped at Thompson Springs RV Park, where teammates cooked a chicken taco dinner.

title: Spokes Day 55: I 70, You 70, We all 70, for I 70
summary: Rode about 9 miles of I-70 shoulder between Glenwood Springs and Rifle CO on purpose. The interstate option (27 miles, 250 ft gain) was preferred over the other route (47 miles, 4,000 ft gain, about 6 hours). The shoulder was wide with a rumble strip, and drivers moved over for the team's high-visibility vests.

title: Day 58: If You Give a Cyclist a Rain Storm
summary: After a rainstorm the team started late and rode 50 miles from Thompson Springs UT to Moab. They stopped at Jackass Joe's Jerky for gas station water and ice cream, rode through Arches National Park, and stayed at the Lazy Lizard Hostel in Moab.

title: Day 60: Today Was ...... MEH
summary: Left Moab on a bike path, then hit one of the worst shoulders of the trip, with trucks, RVs and cars passing every minute. The team called Robert to shuttle them to the end of that road. The rest of the 52-mile day was smooth and they camped at Green River State Park.

title: Day 61: Battling Sand and Night
summary: A hard day: the team left late and was routed onto a sandy, almost non-existent road, then rode in the dark with no phone service and weak front lights. Support car Dora and Simone found them about 10 miles from the campsite. They camped near Capitol Reef with no showers, and a cyclist named James suggested stopping at Mesa Farm Market.

title: Day 64: Trees Growing Out of Rock
summary: Rode 49 miles from Escalante to Bryce Canyon NP on Scenic Byway 12, with trees growing from rock crevices and red, yellow and pink rock cliffs. A thunderstorm caught them; they sheltered at a trailhead bathroom until the support car came. The team also attended a rodeo that evening.

title: Day 65: Year 23
summary: Rest day in the Bryce Canyon area for Maxwell's 23rd birthday. The team had breakfast pies, mountain biked (dropped at the wrong trailhead, then a riverbed detour), toured hoodoos in Bryce Canyon NP, ate a buffet dinner and gave Maxwell a handwritten card.

title: Day 66: The Scenery on This Bike Ride Was The G.O.A.T.s
summary: Rode 74 miles from Bryce Canyon Pines Campground to Cedar City UT past hoodoos, slot canyons, sheep and the Zion Overlook. An unpassable grass road and an ATV trail cost time, and a small cave crawl was part of lunch. The team stayed with Warm Showers hosts Pat and Ken, who hosted a pizza party. The support car got a flat tire that day.

title: Day 67: Tired of Tires... and COVID?
summary: The support car had a flat tire on the descent from Bryce; the team swapped in the spare, then replaced all four tires in Cedar City. Robert tested positive for COVID and was sent to isolate in a Reno hotel, driven across Nevada by Mariela and Amira. Riders slept at Mountain View Baptist Church in Milford UT.

title: Spokes Day 62 + 63: Guy Fieri Was Here (sort of)
summary: Rest day at Capitol Reef NP (goat farm lunch, Curry Pizza dinner), then a 70-mile day with about 6,000 ft of climbing and 6,000 ft of descent into Escalante UT, ending at a lakeside campground.

title: Day 68/69: If You Like Bikes, Honk!
summary: Rode 84 miles from Milford UT to Baker NV, crossing into Pacific Time, then took a rest day in Baker NV (population 36) at the Stargazer Inn hostel and its general store.

title: Day 70: Driving can be fun
summary: Support-car day: the blogger drove while the bikers rode 63 miles from Baker to Ely NV; the team stopped at the Great Basin visitor center and stayed at a La Quinta in Ely, where a planned learning festival had been cancelled due to COVID and they packed goodie bags for kids.

title: Day 71: Not Lonely on The Loneliest Road
summary: Rode US-50 ('the Loneliest Road') from Ely to Eureka NV (78 miles); a thunderstorm soaked the team with cold rain and no cell service meant they could not reach the driver, so they shuttled the last stretch and got ice cream and a Highway 50 stamp in Eureka.

title: Day 72: Into The Void
summary: Biked 63 miles on US-50 from Eureka to Austin NV and saw wild mustangs; a twisted ankle put one rider in the car after 10 miles, and the planned housing fell through when the town park banned overnight camping, so the team stayed at an RV campsite.

title: Day 73: High mileage, high dollar bills
summary: Longest day of the trip: 112 miles from Austin to Fallon NV (2,615 ft of elevation drop per the post) across salt flats and desert, with lunch at Middlegate Station, wild horses running alongside, and arrival at the Fallon Youth Center for a learning festival.

title: Day 74: One last day of rest
Day 75: Last Day of Teaching, First Day of School
summary: Last learning festival of the trip, at the Fallon Youth Club on a Sunday with low turnout (schools started the next day); the team reflected that their workshops moved from content-heavy to hands-on and engagement-driven.

title: Day 76: Where is Robert? And Other Frequently Asked Questions
summary: Fallon to Carson City NV (63 miles, 1,500 ft of gain); the team picked up Robert after his COVID isolation in Reno, rejoined the bikers, and had a rib dinner with host Tod on a hilltop. The post also launched a Q&A for blog readers.

title: Day 77: So Long And Thanks For All the Fish
summary: Carson City NV to Lake Tahoe CA (47 miles, 3,900 ft of gain) with host Tod riding along; camped at Emerald Bay, which had water on both sides; the team also listed the many items lost over the trip.

title: Day 78: Spokes of One Wheel
summary: Rode 103 miles from South Lake Tahoe to Sacramento CA, the team's first six-biker day, with friend Kellie riding 60 miles over the Sierras; a route mistake onto a Highway 50 freeway led to a back-road detour, and the day ended with a church dinner at a host's home in Sacramento.

title: Day 79: There Is So Much To Look Forward To, and You Have No Idea What It Is
summary: Sacramento to Vacaville CA (56 miles, 243 ft of gain) on a river path and bike trails, with an In-N-Out lunch in Davis; the post is a reflection on music played along the trip and on lessons about group living and cycling.

title: Day 80: Oh, the Places You'll Go!
summary: Final ride, Vacaville to San Francisco (73.2 miles, 1,909 ft of gain), finishing over the Golden Gate Bridge at sunset with friends and family waiting; the post also tallies trip totals and names foam sleeping pads as the team's MVP.

title: So. many. degrees. !!!
summary: On a 108-degree day the team rode Hanksville to Hite, UT, sheltered in shade until a 2 a.m. night ride of about 80 miles to Blanding, UT. The post also notes Nathan's video is out and the team is about to cross into Colorado.

title: Home in every town :)
summary: The team rode Telluride to Montrose (a July 4 fireworks night ride), a 106-mile day to Sargent at the base of Monarch Pass (11,312 ft), a KOA, Fairplay, a night inside Bailey's Cutthroat Cafe, a Loveland library Learning Festival, a Boulder break day, and then reached Colorado Springs.

title: A misplaced border
summary: After a northern Colorado detour that added a couple hundred miles, the team rode from Colorado Springs toward Pueblo, took 22 miles of gravel road onto the Transamerica trail, and welcomed Noor Razzak as the ninth team member to document the trip.

title: Is a difficult youth essential for building character?
summary: A reflective post inspired by Roberto Carlos Rivera's talk at the Unreasonable Institute, arguing that adversity builds character and that shielding children from it may leave them hopeless.

title: Cool Kansas :)
summary: The team enjoyed the flat, scenic Kansas riding, visited the Cosmosphere in Hutchinson, had a bike repaired in Newton, and planned to meet an MIT friend who would guest-ride to St. Louis.

title: How to build a trebuchet? Ideas on project-based learning.
summary: At a 24-hour Learning Festival on a Millstadt, Illinois farm, 30 St. Louis homeschool teens brainstormed projects, and one team designed and fired a trebuchet in about five hours. The post reflects on why projects succeeded and where they stalled.

title: Just the tortilla of the burrito that has been the past few weeks
summary: A catch-up recap post (no single day) covering several weeks: a car run-in (everyone ok), a team member leaving and a new one joining, three learning festival sessions, passing the St. Louis Arch and crossing the Missouri and Mississippi rivers, and a stop in Murphysboro, IL, under 1,000 miles from DC with a planned detour south to Nashville.

title: We did it! We're in DC!
summary: The team rode into Washington, DC at 11:24am on August 24, 2013, finishing the Pacific-to-Atlantic ride (post says more than 6,000 km), and planned celebrations, thank-you cards and a post-trip reflection series.
